posts.title: Open day on 16 January: what happens on the morning
posts.excerpt: Our next open day is on Saturday 16 January 2027, from 10:00 to 13:00 at 2 Orchard Row.
posts.content:
Come at ten and Priya Raman, our admissions officer, will meet you at the door. At 10:20 you sit in on a studio session with Owen Gallagher: sand, water and a tray of funnels, tried by adults first.

At 11:15 there is a talk with a practice tutor about what a placement week looks like, and at 12:00 you can ask Priya anything about applying. We close at 13:00. If you would rather see a nursery in session, book a Wednesday tour between 14:00 and 15:30.

posts.title: Ten minutes of only watching
posts.excerpt: On Tuesdays the second-year trainees spend the first ten minutes of the morning saying nothing.
posts.content:
At Fernhill Forest Nursery, Owen Gallagher asks the trainees to sit on the logs and only watch what the children do with the mud kitchen. No questions, no help, no notes until the ten minutes are over.

Then they talk. What did the child with the red pan do before she poured? Who watched whom? The point is not the answers but the habit: noticing first, deciding afterwards.

posts.title: Why we put trainees in a room from week 3
posts.excerpt: Two days a week in a partner nursery, starting in the third week of the course.
posts.content:
Margit Sorensen started the college in 1987 with eight evening students and one rule: you learn the work where it happens. Today every trainee spends two days a week in a partner nursery or reception class from week 3.

Once a week a tutor watches from the doorway and talks it through the same afternoon. It is slower than a lecture and a good deal harder, and it is why the groups stay small.
